abstract: How nuclear mRNAs are selectively packaged into ribonucleoprotein particles (mRNPs) is fundamental to elucidating the mechanisms that govern gene expression. Here, we interrogate nuclear mRNP maturation in S. cerevisiae by combining a proteomic (34 baits) and transcriptomic (18 baits) affinity-purification survey with sequential purification of individual MS2-tagged nuclear transcripts at successive stages of maturation. Contrary to the prevailing models in which nuclear mRNAs are extensively coated with a stable complement of proteins, we find that they share a minimal core of Yra1p and Pab1p, together with a more dynamically associated cap-binding complex. Most other factors associate transiently and transcript-selectively, assembling as pre-assembled, stage-specific modules. The minimal core is invariant to promoter, coding sequence and transcript length, whereas intron class, rather than intron presence alone, determines spliceosome composition. The breadth of factor association further tracks promoter class and proximity to chromatin-domain boundaries, linking mRNP biogenesis to genome organization.
